comparison: Perfect agreement on antibiotic tolerance phenotype claims (C1, C33-C39, C78). Both evaluations find the experimental data convincing and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes the experimental methodology and controls, while peer reviewers affirm the findings as valuable and convincing.

Strong agreement on claims challenging PMF-dependent mechanism (C2, C3, C40, C43-C46, C48, C73). OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple experimental approaches, while peer reviewers explicitly support the challenge to established dogma and appreciate clarifications about not refuting PMF-dependent uptake. Peer review R2 also includes membrane potential claims (C53-C55) that OpenEval addresses separately in R7.

Complete agreement on TCA cycle upregulation and compensatory mechanisms (C4, C5, C56-C62). Both evaluations accept the proteomics findings without challenge. OpenEval provides detailed mechanistic interpretation, while peer reviewers describe the study as complete and convincing.

Full agreement on ribosomal downregulation mechanism (C6-C10, C63-C66, C79). Both evaluations affirm this as a key mechanistic finding explaining aminoglycoside tolerance. OpenEval emphasizes the mechanistic consistency with drug targets, while peer reviewers accept it as part of the convincing overall results.

Agreement on differential behavior of Δicd mutant (C67-C68). Both evaluations accept this negative control result. OpenEval emphasizes its value in strengthening conclusions through correlation analysis, while peer reviewers implicitly accept it as part of the complete and convincing study.

Agreement on MIC measurements distinguishing tolerance from resistance (C35). Both evaluations recognize this as an important control. OpenEval explicitly notes its importance for phenotype distinction, while peer reviewers implicitly accept it by affirming the overall tolerance mechanism findings.

Partial overlap on membrane potential claims (C53-C55). OpenEval R7 focuses specifically on DiSC3(5) measurements showing no PMF differences, while peer R2 groups these with broader PMF-mechanism claims (C2, C3, C40, C43-C46, C48, C73). Both evaluations support the findings, with peer reviewers appreciating lower concentration experiments.

OpenEval R8 addresses methodological validation claim (C52) about gentamicin's effect on membrane potential as assay control. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers accepted overall methodology without specifically commenting on this validation.

Partial overlap on pH measurements (C74). OpenEval R9 specifically addresses lack of acidification distinguishing this work from prior studies, while peer R7 broadly addresses contextualization with prior literature (C69-C72, C74, C76-C77). Both evaluations support the appropriate comparison with previous work.

OpenEval R10 addresses background knowledge claims (C11-C32) establishing context from existing literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not specifically comment on background claims, focusing instead on novel findings.

Strong agreement on contextualization with prior work (C69-C72, C76-C77). OpenEval emphasizes appropriate citation usage for comparison, while peer reviewers accept how findings relate to previous work without contradicting established mechanisms. Peer R7 also includes C74 which OpenEval addresses separately in R9.

OpenEval R12 addresses gene function distinction claim (C75). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not specifically comment on this technical distinction between soluble and membrane-bound proteins.

OpenEval R13 addresses methodological validation claims (C41-C42, C49-C51) about assay mechanisms. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers accepted methodology without specifically commenting on these technical validations.

Perfect agreement on concentration-dependent effects (C47). Both evaluations support the lower concentration experiments. OpenEval notes appropriate consideration of concentration effects with citation, while peer reviewer explicitly requested and appreciates these additional experiments as a considerable improvement.

Complete agreement on overall conclusion about mechanism complexity (C80). Both evaluations affirm the study's contribution. OpenEval emphasizes the shift from PMF-dependent to ribosomal downregulation mechanism, while peer reviewers describe findings as valuable for challenging dogma and contributing to understanding tolerance complexity.
